title: Sales Development Representative
description:
We Breathe Life Into Data

At Komodo Health, our mission is to reduce the global burden of disease. And we believe that smarter use of data is essential to this mission. That’s why we built the Healthcare Map — the industry’s largest, most complete, precise view of the U.S. healthcare system — by combining de-identified, real-world patient data with innovative algorithms and decades of clinical experience. The Healthcare Map serves as our foundation for a powerful suite of software applications, helping us answer healthcare’s most complex questions for our partners. Across the healthcare ecosystem, we’re helping our clients unlock critical insights to track detailed patient behaviors and treatment patterns, identify gaps in care, address unmet patient needs, and reduce the global burden of disease. 

As we pursue these goals, it remains essential to us that we stay grounded in our values: be awesome, seek growth, deliver “wow,” and enjoy the ride. At Komodo, you will be joining a team of ambitious, supportive Dragons with diverse backgrounds but a shared passion to deliver on our mission to reduce the burden of disease — and enjoy the journey along the way.

The Opportunity at Komodo Health

The Sales Development team is the engine of our sales pipeline. Your work will directly support our mission by identifying, engaging, and developing new sales opportunities through proactive outreach to prospective customers. You'll be a critical part of the Revenue team, creating the foundational relationships that translate into strategic partnerships and business growth for Komodo Health. 

This role is a prime launchpad for a successful career in health-tech sales and an opportunity to be at the forefront of bringing innovative products to market, including MarmotAI.

As a Sales Development Representative (SDR), you will play a key role partnering with the sales organization to identify and develop new, high-quality sales opportunities in the Payers, Providers, and Digital Health space. You will serve as the crucial first point of contact, setting the stage for successful engagement between prospective customers and our sellers. 

Looking back on your first 12 months at Komodo Health, you will have…

  • Exceeded Monthly Targets: Consistently met or exceeded monthly targets for completed meetings with key personas across the most innovative companies in healthcare.
  • Drive Pipeline Progression: Consistently met or exceeded monthly targets for opportunities progressing through the sales pipeline, demonstrating the high quality of your lead generation efforts.
  • Mastered Territory: Developed a deep working knowledge of your assigned territory and the value proposition of Komodo Health's solutions within it.

You will accomplish these outcomes through the following responsibilities...

  • Partnership: Partner closely with stakeholders in Sales to deeply understand target accounts, ideal customer profiles (ICPs), and the specific value Komodo Health brings to their challenges.
  • Strategic Targeting: Receive and incorporate continuous feedback and coaching on cutting-edge outbound prospecting methods and completed meetings to refine strategy and drive measurable impact.
  • Pipeline Generation: Execute sophisticated lead generation campaigns, including coordination of introductory meetings, qualification calls, and product demonstrations with key prospects to showcase Komodo’s capabilities and solutions.
  • Opportunity Conversion: Translate strategic outreach and defined account plans into tangible, qualified opportunities that drive pipeline progression for the sales organization.
  • AI-Powered Efficiency: Leverage Generative AI (GenAI) tools and other sales technology to streamline or automate aspects of your workflow, such as drafting personalized initial outreach emails, synthesizing research on target accounts, and continuously refining message resonance for optimal response rates.
  • Data-Driven Outreach: Maintain an acute understanding of targeting outreach that converts into real, high-quality opportunities for sellers, ensuring all efforts are focused on maximum impact.

What you bring to Komodo Health (required):

  • At least 2-3 years of experience in an SDR or BDR domain demonstrating the ability to quickly grasp complex technical and industry concepts.
  • Strong foundational knowledge in top-of-funnel sales and outbound prospecting.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with a proven ability to articulate complex ideas clearly and persuasively.
  • Fluency in English (written and spoken).
  • Sales Drive: A genuine passion for sales, relationship building, and achieving ambitious goals.
  • Tech Savvy: Familiarity with the use of technology, including AI/GenAI tools (i.e., Clay), to streamline, automate, or enhance lead generation and research activities.
  • Strategic Mindset: A proactive and analytical understanding of targeted outreach strategies that demonstrably convert into high-quality, actionable opportunities for sellers.

Additional skills and experience we’ll prioritize…

  • Experience in prospecting and generating leads in the Digital Health, Specialty Pharma, or Payers/Providers industry.
  • Experience with Salesforce, Salesloft, and/or Qualified.io.

title: Real World Data Analyst
description:
Real World Data Analyst

Truveta transforms healthcare into intelligence. Built with and owned by US health systems united by a mission of Saving Lives with Data, Truveta powers breakthrough discoveries, auditable data fit for regulatory submissions, and AI that improves patient care.

At Truveta, we are building something that has never existed before, bringing together healthcare, science, and technology to tackle some of the most important challenges in human health. Our mission calls us to think big, move with urgency, and build with purpose. We are looking for exceptional people who are energized by hard problems, inspired by the opportunity to improve health, and committed to building a company and culture where talented people can do their best work.

Our team is a special combination of software, health, and big data experience. We are building a talented team of passionate, mission-oriented, and innovative thinkers. 

Truveta was born in the Pacific Northwest, but we have employees who live across the country.  Our team enjoys the flexibility of a hybrid model and working from anywhere.  In person attendance is required at least once per year for an onsite meeting. 

For overall team productivity, we optimize meeting hours in the pacific time zone. We avoid scheduling recurring meetings that start after 3pm PT, however, ad hoc meetings occur between 8am-6pm Pacific time. #LI-remote

Who We Need 

Truveta is rapidly building a talented and diverse team to tackle complex health and technical challenges. Beyond core capabilities, we are seeking problem solvers, passionate and collaborative teammates, and those willing to roll up their sleeves while making a difference. If you are interested in the opportunity to pursue purposeful work, join a mission-driven team, and build a rewarding career while having fun, Truveta may be the perfect fit for you. 

This Opportunity

 

The Real World Data Analyst role is a high-impact, intellectually challenging position that requires a diverse set of analytical and technical skills. It offers a unique opportunity for professional growth through access to an unprecedented volume of high-quality, real-world Electronic Health Record (EHR) data. In this role, you will tackle meaningful healthcare challenges using an EHR database encompassing more than 125 million patients—and growing—helping drive insights that can ultimately improve patient care. This position reports to the Senior Director of Research Services. 

As a Real World Data Analyst, you will collaborate strategically with some of our largest life sciences partners. This role provides the opportunity to dive deeply into complex research questions related to human health and generate data-driven insights that support impactful scientific decisions.  

Responsibilities

  • Translate study protocols and statistical analysis plans (SAPs) into reproducible analytical code, executing end-to-end research studies from data extraction and wrangling through statistical analysis and results generation using SQL, R, or Python within agreed timelines. 
  • Review and interpret study protocols and SAPs, ensuring analytical approaches are implemented accurately and consistently with study objectives. 
  • Develop robust data pipelines for cohort building, data cleaning, feature engineering, and preparation of analytical datasets using large-scale real-world data sources. 
  • Conduct rigorous quality control (QC) of code, datasets, and statistical outputs, including verification of model assumptions, reproducibility of results, and validation of analytical approaches. 
  • Proactively identify and communicate potential data issues, methodological concerns, or deviations from study protocols early in the research process, recommending solutions and mitigation strategies. 
  • Collaborate closely with biostatisticians and researchers to support the development, refinement, and review of statistical analysis plans and analytical methods. 
  • Interpret analytical results and contribute to the synthesis of findings, ensuring outputs are scientifically sound and aligned with study objectives. 
  • Partner with life sciences customers and internal teams to execute high-quality analyses that support peer-reviewed publications, regulatory submissions, and scientific research.  
  • Present and interpret statistical findings to a wide range of internal and external partners across a variety of technical levels. 
  • Provide clear, proactive communication on study progress, analytical challenges, and timelines, ensuring all partners remain informed and aligned. 
  • Work closely with cross-functional teams across Truveta to investigate data sources, validate data integrity, and support scientific credibility of research outputs. 
  • Deliver feedback to internal teams based on research experiences and customer needs to help inform improvements to Truveta’s data platform and research capabilities. 

Required Skills

  • Undergraduate or graduate degree in biostatistics, epidemiology, clinical research, data science, clinical informatics, or a related field. 
  • 3+ years of experience conducting analyses using large healthcare datasets (e.g., electronic health records or other real-world data sources). 
  • Strong proficiency in SQL and at least one statistical programming language (R or Python) for data wrangling, analysis, and reproducible research workflows. 
  • Experience translating research protocols or statistical analysis plans into executable analytical code. 
  • Experience performing rigorous quality control of analytical datasets, code, and statistical outputs. 
  • Demonstrated experience working with complex healthcare data involving millions of patient records. 
  • Experience collaborating with research teams or customers to deliver high-quality scientific analyses. 
  • Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to identify data or methodological issues early and communicate them effectively. 
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to clearly explain analytical approaches and findings to technical and non-technical partners. 
  • Ability to learn quickly and adapt in a dynamic, fast-paced environment. 
  • Willingness to learn new analytical tools, programming languages, and proprietary platforms used to analyze real-world data. 

Preferred Qualifications

These qualifications are preferred but not required, please do not let them stop you from applying for this role. You will likely get the opportunity to learn how to do these more advanced analyses if you don’t already have experience with them.  

  • Experience applying causal inference methods to observational healthcare data, including approaches such as propensity score matching/weighting, inverse probability weighting, marginal structural models, or instrumental variable analysis. 
  • Familiarity with study designs used to estimate causal effects in real-world data, such as target trial emulation, difference-in-differences, regression discontinuity, or interrupted time series. 
  • Experience evaluating confounding, selection bias, and other threats to causal validity in observational studies. 
  • Ability to work flexibly across different project timelines, including responding to emerging or time-sensitive analytic needs. 

Why Truveta?   

Be a part of building something special. Now is the perfect time to join Truveta. We have strong, established leadership with decades of success. We are well-funded. We are building a culture that prioritizes people and their passions across personal, professional and everything in between. Join us as we build an amazing company together.  

We Offer:

  • Interesting and meaningful work for every career stage
  • Great benefits package
  • Comprehensive benefits with strong medical, dental and vision insurance plans
  • 401K plan
  • Professional development & training opportunities for continuous learning
  • Work/life autonomy via flexible work hours and flexible paid time off
  • Generous parental leave
  • Regular team activities (virtual and in-person)
  • The base pay for this position is $110,000 to $160,000. The pay range reflects the minimum and maximum target. Pay is based on several factors including location and may vary depending on job-related knowledge, skills, and experience.  This role is eligible for stock options.

If you are based in California, we encourage you to read this important information for California residents linked here.

Truveta is committed to creating a diverse, inclusive, and empowering workplace. We believe that having employees, interns, and contractors with diverse backgrounds enables Truveta to better meet our mission and serve patients and health communities around the world. We recognize that opportunities in technology historically excluded and continue to disproportionately exclude Black and Indigenous people, people of color, people from working class backgrounds, people with disabilities, and LGBTQIA+ people. We strongly encourage individuals with these identities to apply even if you don’t meet all of the requirements.

Please note that all applicants must be authorized to work in the United States for any employer as we are unable to sponsor work visas or permits (e.g. F-1 OPT, H1-B) at this time. We appreciate your interest in the position and encourage you to explore future opportunities with us.

About the Role: 

Care Delivery is the infrastructure that powers how Maven members access care and how our providers deliver it. Every program we run across maternity, fertility, menopause, and pediatrics, depends on it. It's where clinical workflows, provider tooling, and the systems that make care measurable, billable, and scalable at Maven's scale all come together.

We're looking for a Product Manager to help build that platform: the EHR and clinical tooling, provider workflows, messaging, and the data and billing infrastructure that turn Maven's care model into something reliable and scalable. You'll own defined capabilities within the platform and drive them from problem to shipped, in close partnership with engineering, clinical, design, and operations. It's a high-leverage seat. What you build here touches every program Maven offers.

You'll report to the Group Product Manager, Care Delivery, and work closely with our providers, as well as Clinical Product, Member Experience, Operations, and the Data and AI Platform teams.

What You’ll Do:

  • Own specific Care Delivery capabilities end-to-end, provider workflows, clinical documentation, messaging, scheduling and matching, or quality and billing infrastructure, from problem definition through launch and iteration.
  • Make crisp, well-reasoned product decisions, especially where clinical accuracy and provider experience are both at stake.
  • Use AI hands-on to move faster, prototyping with AI tools to test ideas and pressure-test flows before committing engineering time, and identify and build AI-powered capabilities into the care delivery platform where they genuinely improve the provider or member experience.
  • Partner daily with engineering and design to ship reliable platform capabilities, and with clinical and operations partners so that what you build works for real providers and members.
  • Translate regulatory and quality requirements, like HEDIS measures and clinical coding, into clean product experiences that add value without adding friction.
  • Instrument what you ship, watch how it performs, and iterate. Bring data to every decision.
  • Build platform primitives, reusable capabilities that serve many programs, rather than one-off features.
  • Bring a point of view on how AI can improve care delivery workflows, and put it to work in how you build.

What You’ll Bring: 

  • 3+ years in product management, ideally with some time in healthcare tech or another complex, regulated, or operations-heavy domain.
  • A strong executor: you take ambiguous problems, break them down, and ship, without needing everything defined for you.
  • Solid data instincts: you define the right metrics, work with real datasets, and communicate findings clearly to both clinical and commercial audiences.
  • Comfort with technical and clinical complexity: you can hold your own in an engineering sprint and a clinical review, and you're eager to learn the domain fast (FHIR, interoperability, EHR workflows).
  • Genuine care for providers and members: the people using what you build show up in your decisions.
  • Clear, direct communication and strong cross-functional collaboration.
  • Fluency with AI and a genuine desire to build with it: you understand how modern AI models work well enough to know where they're reliable and where they aren't, you reach for AI tools to prototype and think, and you're excited to ship AI-powered features rather than just talk about them.
  • Bonus: experience with EHR or EMR systems, clinical workflows, healthcare interoperability, or provider-facing tools.

title: AI Imaging Specialist - Radiology
description: Latch builds rigorous scientific benchmarks ( benchmarks.bio ) for AI agents across biology. We work with frontier labs and pharma to measure whether agents can handle real biological workflows: the messy, multi-layer reasoning that matters in the field. AI agents can now work through an imaging study the way a radiologist does: open the dataset, explore the dataset based on an indication, identify relevant features based on experience and tools and validate findings. Having agents being involved in the interpretation of clinical samples or even in the diagnosis of patients requires enormous care as well as validation of capability, but also offers massive advantages for patient care. We're building RadiologyBench and are looking for people who work with medical images every day, whether you read studies or acquire them. About the Role You’ll decide what the right answer is for each case and build the studies that test it, from whether a scan was acquired properly to what shows. You then go through how AI agents actually handled them, including what they missed and what they reported that isn’t there. Labs use these results to see where their models fall short of an expert. The work covers MRI, CT, ultrasound and radiography, across organ systems. Designing the task Write the questions that are frequently asked by radiologists or during interpretation of medical images Decide on the optimal answer format that the agent should use Decide what counts as a pass given the objective Review what agents are actually doing and if their approach holds up Help pick what is actually needed by the agent to solve the objective Requirements Can work with medical images professionally and have handled thousands of studies, your role could include: Radiologist, including trained outside the US (board-certified or equivalent) Radiology resident or fellow Sonographer (ARDMS or equivalent) MRI or CT technologist (ARRT or equivalent) Deep experience in at least one modality (MRI, CT, ultrasound or radiography) and working familiarity with the others You know normal anatomy and common pathology for your area, and you can tell when the image itself is wrong: artifact, positioning, parameters Comfortable enough to work with python on interpretation and run scripts. No specific ML engineering is required but could come in handy AI-ready, daily use of popular agents like Claude Code, with judgement to distinguish between technical correctness but clinical unsoundness Bonus: imaging AI challenge experience ( e.g. RSNA, MICCAI, …) or contributions e.g. to Radiopaedia Bonus: familiarity with public imaging archives (TCIA, MIMIC-CXR, UK Biobank, OpenNeuro) Compensation $140K–$180K OTE (on-target earnings), with no ceiling. Your pay is your OTE times your weekly quota attainment. Hit quota, earn your OTE; double it, earn double. Example: $150K OTE at double quota = $300K. Your first 4 weeks (ramp) are paid at full OTE while you learn our workflows. You’re paid full OTE whenever quota can’t fairly apply: when a new project is starting, the platform goes down, or we pull you onto a special project. Benefits & Employment In the US: full-time W-2 Guaranteed floor (“base salary”) set by your state, paid on the 15th and last day of every month Health, dental, vision: 100% covered for you, 50% for dependents 401(k) (no match) PTO: 15 days to start, more as you’re promoted Outside the US: contractor Paid on performance. We want our team to have stability, so we pay 60% of your monthly OTE up front as an advance, balanced against your earnings in later paychecks. US benefits don’t apply. Growth Two tracks, based on output. Individual contributor: six levels, so up to five promotions, with OTE rising at each one. Management: after your first promotion, you can move into managing a pod or keep growing on the IC track. Location & Work Authorization Location: remote or onsite at our Mission Bay office in San Francisco. Onsite is preferred: working side by side is how we share knowledge and keep our work rigorous. We have a global team, and remote teammates regularly visit the office. Work authorization: we sponsor H-1B (new and transfers), O-1, and TN, and support STEM OPT. Culture @ Latch We practice radical transparency: you’ll know how the company is doing, what’s working, and what isn’t. It’s always us against the problem, never each other. We’re opinionated but respectful of each other’s time, and we think through possible solutions before bringing a problem to anyone. We use AI constantly, so we reward original expert judgment, not AI output passed off as your own. You’ll start on the bench that fits your expertise and can move across teams as you build a track record. Outside of work: company outings most months, team off-sites, and a community that does cycling, soccer, figure skating, boxing, running, martial arts, music, books, and game nights. Interview Process Apply. If your profile matches, we’ll send you a take-home project. Take-home project (HackerRank). We review it as soon as it arrives. Technical interview with a Member of Technical Staff (pod lead). Culture interview with our C-suite. Offer. Background check, once you accept.

title: Member of Technical Staff, Clinical Data & Statistical Programming
description: Member of Technical Staff, Clinical Data & Statistical Programming Our mission is to advance humanity's ability to engineer biology. We approach this by understanding and improving AI’s application to biology across basic research, drug discovery, and biosecurity. We are a team of engineers, scientists, and operations specialists who are driven by improving capabilities and interpretability. Some of our work is showcased on benchmarks.bio . About this role. You will build evaluations of the work that turns clinical protocols and study records into trustworthy datasets and reproducible results. The role has two tracks: Clinical data management: Designing data collection, configuring study databases, and managing queries, reconciliation, and data quality. Statistical programming: Writing and validating code in SAS, R, or Python to construct analysis datasets, implement prespecified analyses, and produce clinical-trial tables, listings, and figures. We welcome candidates with depth in either track. Your initial roadmap will draw on that expertise, with the broader function growing through collaboration and hiring. This is a high-intensity, founder-type role. Our Members of Technical Staff have built companies, run drug programs and scaled complex technical projects. What you will do: - Build evaluations around data-capture requirements, database logic, edit checks, queries, and reconciliation across study sources. - Develop tasks that test agents writing and validating code for analysis-dataset construction, derivations, traceability, and production of clinical-trial tables, listings, and figures. - Create reference outputs and checks that identify consequential errors in data processing and programmed analyses. - Work with engineers to run agents and investigate whether outputs are correct, reproducible, and consistent with study requirements. - Build the first evaluations yourself, then recruit and lead experts across the function's complementary specialties. What we look for: - Substantial experience delivering clinical databases, study datasets, or programmed analyses for real studies. - Depth in at least one track: clinical data management or statistical programming. Experience across both is valuable but not required. - The ability to work directly with underlying records, identify inconsistencies, and explain the consequences of processing choices. Statistical programming candidates should have strong hands-on coding ability in SAS, R, or Python, including validation and reproducibility. - Scientific curiosity, comfort learning AI tools, and the judgment and initiative to build a team responsible for high-quality output. We welcome scientists who have become fluent with AI tools and quantitative or engineering researchers with substantial hands-on experience in the relevant domain. How we work. Our MTS team works in person in Mission Bay, San Francisco. We keep meetings to a minimum and are flexible about when you arrive or leave. You’ll work across Sales, Marketing, Product, Solutions Architecture, and regional partnerships teams to develop shared opportunities and turn them into scalable global partner strategies.

Although the role sits on the Americas Alliances and Channels Tech Partnerships team, its mandate is global. title: Delivery Excellence Lead - Medical Communications
description:
About Avalere Health

United by one profound purpose: to reach EVERY PATIENT POSSIBLE. At Avalere Health, we ensure every patient is identified, treated, supported, and cared for. Equally. Our Advisory, Medical, and Marketing teams come together – powerfully and intentionally – to forge unconventional connections, building a future where healthcare is not a barrier and no patient is left behind. 

Achieving our mission starts with providing enriching, purpose-driven careers for our team that empower them to make a tangible impact on patient lives. We are committed to creating a culture where our employees are empowered to bring their whole selves to work and tap into the power of diverse backgrounds and skillsets to play a part in making a difference for every patient, everywhere. 

Our flexible approach to working allows our global teams to decide where they want to work, whether in-office or at home based on team and client need. Major city hubs in London, Manchester, Washington, D.C., and New York, and smaller offices globally, serve as collaboration hubs allowing our teams to come together when it matters. Homeworkers are equally supported, with dedicated social opportunities and resources.  

Our inclusive culture is at the heart of everything we do. We proudly support our employees in bringing their whole selves to work with our six Employee Network Groups – Diverse Ability, Family, Gender, LGBTQ+, Mental Health, and Race/Ethnicity. These groups provide opportunities to promote diversity, equity, and inclusion and to connect, learn, and socialise through regular meetings and programs of activity. We are an accredited Fertility Friendly employer with our Fertility Policy, enhanced parental leave, and culture of flexibility ensuring every employee feels supported across their family planning journey and can work in a way that suits their family’s needs. 

We are deeply invested in supporting professional growth for our employees through day-to-day career experiences, access to thousands of on-demand training sessions, regular career conversations, and the opportunity for global, cross-capability career moves.  

We take pride in being part of the Disability Confident Scheme. This helps make sure you can be interviewed fairly if you have a disability, long term health condition, or are neurodiverse. If you'd like to apply and need adjustments made, you can let us know in your application.


Location: UK, flexible, hybrid or remote.

You will lead client service and delivery excellence, operational efficiency and AI-enabled transformation across our Medical division, with accountability for driving sustained improvement across key commercial measures including utilisation, recoveries and revenue per hour.
 
Reporting to the President, Medical, you will play a pivotal role in shaping how we deliver for our clients and operate as a business. You will establish scalable, commercially effective delivery models that strengthen client experience, productivity and profitability, partnering with Business Unit Leaders and functional teams to embed consistent delivery standards, optimise resources and accelerate the adoption of technology, including Workfront.
 
You will provide strategic leadership for the operating discipline that underpins successful delivery, working with the Head of Operations across five core areas: resource planning, delivery structure, project administration, client delivery excellence, and reporting and insight.
 
This role will suit a senior leader with significant experience in Medical or Healthcare Communications and/or Healthcare Consulting who is passionate about transforming how complex, client-led businesses deliver. You’ll be energised by the opportunity to influence at the highest level, challenge established ways of working and create scalable, technology-enabled approaches that strengthen client experience, operational excellence and commercial performance.
 What we can offer You'll receive up to a 7% pension contribution, life insurance, income protection, and private medical insurance for peace of mind. Enjoy flexible working arrangements, including flexible hybrid working, along with the option to work from anywhere across the globe two weeks each year. We provide 25 days of annual leave plus two personal well-being days, along with gifted end-of-year holidays and an early Summer Friday finish in June, July, and August. Access free counselling through our employee assistance program, as well as personalized health support. Enhanced maternity, paternity, family leave, and fertility policies provide support across every stage of your family-planning journey, as well as on-demand support from our partner Peppy. You can also benefit from continuous opportunities to professionally develop with on-demand training, support, and global mobility opportunities across the business. We encourage all applicants to read our candidate privacy notice before applying to Avalere Health.

title: Project Manager, Medical Affairs
description:
At Real Chemistry, making the world a healthier place isn’t just an aspiration—it’s our everyday reality. Our drive to transform healthcare is informed by our blend of deep scientific expertise, human-centered creativity, and AI-driven insights, fostering a unique environment where innovation thrives and our people are impact-obsessed. As a global agency, we provide a full suite of services across healthcare communications and marketing to our clients, including top players in the pharmaceutical and biotech industries.

Our #LifeatRealChem culture is rooted in our people—we believe we are best together and are committed to excellence for both our clients and colleagues. Whether you're a seasoned professional or just starting your career, if you share our passion for healthcare and connection, we invite you to explore our opportunities.

Discover your purpose. Embrace innovation. Experience #LifeatRealChem.

Real Chemistry is looking for a Project Manager to join our growing Medical Affairs team!  

The Project Manager is responsible for delivering assigned medical affairs projects from initiation through final closeout, including planning, coordination, budget management, routing, approvals, and launch of project deliverables. Projects may include slide decks, print projects, congress materials, advisory board materials, scientific communications, and smaller digital initiatives. This role serves as a main point of contact across internal and external teams, partnering closely with Account, Scientific/Medical, Editorial, Creative, Studio, Print Production, User Experience, Technology, and Quality Assurance partners to keep work on time, on budget, and aligned to client expectations.

Whether it’s bringing in the right resources at the right time, aligning priorities with the account team, or identifying bottlenecks and proposing solutions early, no two days are the same.  

This is a hybrid role, based in any of our US offices—including New York City, Boston, Chicago or Indianapolis—or remotely within the US, depending on team and business needs. This role will primarily work Eastern business hours.

What you’ll do:  

  • Clearly communicate expectations to internal teams and vendors to support the efficient flow of work throughout the agency.
  • Partner with key agency teams to ensure projects stay on track and agreed-upon milestones are met, including Account, Scientific/Medical, Editorial, Creative, Studio, Print Production, Strategic Planning, Information UX, Technology, and Programming teams.
  • Plan, schedule, and monitor work to meet timeline, budget, and quality goals in accordance with relevant guidelines. 
  • Collaborate with finance and accounting teams on revenue recognition/invoicing processes 
  • Participate in client and stakeholder meetings as needed, with a clear understanding of project status and timelines to respond to relevant questions and provide project updates when appropriate.
  • Perform risk planning and mitigation to minimize project risk. 
  • Help create service or departmental standard operating procedures 
  • Route deliverables to appropriate core team members for review and signoff via the electronic project routing system.  
  • Ensure signoff prior to key milestones, including core team review, medical/scientific review, client review, vendor handoff, and final release.
  • Develop detailed work plans, schedules, and status reports to keep internal teams, clients, and external partners aligned throughout the project life cycle. 
  • Serve as a day-to-day project lead, helping define scope and objectives while motivating cross-functional teams to deliver high-quality work on time and on budget. 
  • Coordinate project deliverables from concept through delivery, ensuring the appropriate internal departments, reviews, approvals, and handoffs are engaged at each stage. 
  • Support adherence to agency process and manage the quality assurance phase for all projects.

This position is a perfect fit for you if:  

  • Our Company values – Best Together, Impact-Obsessed, Excellence Expected, Evolve Always and Accountability with an “I” – really speak to you.
  • You are adaptable, resilient, and OK with adjusting your scope, responsibilities, and focus as we grow. When things change, so do we. We’re always evolving.
  • You are proactive, driven, and resourceful with strong prioritization skills and a desire to dive into the data.
  • You are a highly organized self-starter who can work independently and manage tight deadlines.

What you should have:  

  • 3+ years of Project/Program Management or relevant experience. 
  • 2+ years of experience in budget management. 
  • Working familiarity with industry-specific processes, including medical, legal, regulatory, and client review.
  • Background working on teams focused on medical affairs, scientific communications, medical education, or related non-promotional healthcare communications projects.
  • Demonstrated track record of leading small- to medium-scale projects from conception through completion. 
  • Experience working cross-functionally with medical/scientific, editorial, account, creative, and project management partners to deliver high-quality products and services. 
  • Proficient in creating timelines and tracking progress against schedules.
  • Ability to communicate clearly and concisely with technical and non-technical teams across multiple business areas; excellent written, verbal, presentation, and interpersonal skills.

 Pay Range: $70,000-$85,000

This is the pay range the Company believes it will pay for this position at the time of this posting.  Consistent with applicable law, compensation will be determined based on job-related, non-discriminatory factors including but not limited to work experience, skills, certifications, and geographical location. The Company reserves the right to modify this pay range at any time.

You’ll build with your partner teams, not simply deliver solutions to them. You’ll help colleagues move from a manual workflow, to a first AI-enabled win, to a reliable solution they can confidently operate and improve themselves. Success means the workflow stays transformed after the initial build, the team trusts the output, and the people closest to the process can own what comes next. 

You’ll favor learning through building. When possible, you’ll put a useful prototype in front of a Finance user, test it against a real deliverable, and improve it quickly rather than spend weeks describing a theoretical future state. When you encounter platform limitations—which you will—you’ll find creative, supportable approaches, collaborate with Engineering to scope and test custom tools, and escalate strategically when needed.

This role requires a blend of process automation, data operations, technical problem-solving, and stakeholder enablement. You'll spend your time building agents, optimizing data pipelines that feed them, creating knowledge layers that make them more accurate, and training Finance teams to use and maintain them. Success means Finance teams can independently run agents you've built while you provide light support and focus on the next automation opportunity.

Responsibilities

  • Embed with Finance teams to diagnose workflows, identify high-leverage opportunities, and translate business, data, and control requirements into practical AI and automation solutions.

POSITION SUMMARY:  On site position in Austin, TX

Clinical Data Operator accessions patient samples according to standard operating procedures (SOP) with high efficiency and accuracy.  Hourly rate starts at $18.
 
Shift Options:
Tuesday - Saturday,  7am-330pm 
Tuesday - Saturday, 11am-730pm
Hourly rate starts at $18
     
 
PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES

*Front-end lab operations*
- Receive, sort, and transport packages from the shipping dock and reception to the Accessioning lab, and scan tracking numbers accurately.
- Open, prep, and de-kit samples, checking that paperwork matches samples and that no PHI or samples remain in discarded kit boxes.
- Rack bulk samples and distribute work to stations according to distribution guidelines.
- Support sample pickup, consolidation, and send-outs.
- Scan requisitions, bench worksheets, and supporting documents, and upload them to the correct case.
- File, store, and dispose of requisition forms according to retention requirements.
- Empty bins, carts, trash, and biohazard containers, and keep workstations and lab areas clean and organized.

*Case creation and data entry*
- Capture requisition and case information using intelligent document processing (IDP) tools such as Fusion.
- As trained: create new orders in the Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS), enter and review patient data, and keep records accurate and up to date.
- As trained: accession samples across product types with high accuracy and efficiency.

*Quality, safety, and compliance*
- Handle samples (blood, buccal, and tissue) and package-opening tools safely and correctly.
- Escalate packaging issues, discrepancies, or quality concerns to Leads or Supervisors.
- Follow SOPs, quality standards, and safety requirements, including the use of personal protective equipment (PPE).
- This role works with PHI regularly in both paper and electronic form, and has access to various technologies to access PHI in order to do the job. Protect PHI at all times in line with HIPAA and privacy policies.
- Complete HIPAA/PHI privacy, General Policies and Procedure Compliance, and security training as soon as possible, and no later than 30 days after hire.
- Maintain current status on all Natera training requirements.
- Perform other duties as assigned.

**PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS AND WORK ENVIRONMENT**
- Stand and walk for most of the shift, up to 8–10 hours.
- Lift, carry, push, and pull up to 50 lbs regularly, including boxes, totes, and loaded carts.
- Bend, reach, stoop, and kneel repeatedly.
- Perform repetitive hand and wrist motions, including scanning, opening packages, and typing.
- Work in a clinical lab environment with possible exposure to biological samples and biohazardous materials, using required PPE.
- Work in a fast-paced, high-volume, deadline-driven environment.
- Be flexible for shift changes, weekends, holidays, and overtime based on business needs.

**QUALIFICATIONS**
- High school diploma (or equivalent) required.
- 0–1 year of experience in a lab, warehouse, logistics, healthcare, or data entry setting preferred.
- Previous computer experience required.

**KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES**
- Strong attention to detail and accuracy in high-volume, physical work.
- Willingness to do hands-on tasks of every kind as part of a team.
- Ability to learn several workflows and systems, and build toward full accessioning.
- Typing speed of at least 45 wpm with high accuracy, or the ability to reach it during training.
- Good oral and written communication skills, and sound judgment.
- Reliable, organized, self-motivated, and able to work well with others.

OUR OPPORTUNITY

Natera™ is a global leader in cell-free DNA (cfDNA) testing, dedicated to oncology, women’s health, and organ health. Our aim is to make personalized genetic testing and diagnostics part of the standard of care to protect health and enable earlier and more targeted interventions that lead to longer, healthier lives.

The Natera team consists of highly dedicated statisticians, geneticists, doctors, laboratory scientists, business professionals, software engineers and many other professionals from world-class institutions, who care deeply for our work and each other. When you join Natera, you’ll work hard and grow quickly. Working alongside the elite of the industry, you’ll be stretched and challenged, and take pride in being part of a company that is changing the landscape of genetic disease management.

WHAT WE OFFER

Competitive Benefits - Employee benefits include comprehensive medical, dental, vision, life and disability plans for eligible employees and their dependents. Additionally, Natera employees and their immediate families receive free testing in addition to fertility care benefits. Other benefits include pregnancy and baby bonding leave, 401k benefits, commuter benefits and much more. We also offer a generous employee referral program!

For more information, visit www.natera.com.

Natera is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to ensuring a diverse and inclusive workplace environment, and welcome people of different backgrounds, experiences, abilities and perspectives. Inclusive collaboration benefits our employees, our community and our patients, and is critical to our mission of changing the management of disease worldwide.

All qualified applicants are encouraged to apply, and will be considered without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, age, veteran status, disability or any other legally protected status. We also consider qualified applicants regardless of criminal histories, consistent with applicable laws.

If you are based in California, we encourage you to read this important information for California residents. 

Link: https://www.natera.com/notice-of-data-collection-california-residents/

Please be advised that Natera will reach out to candidates with a @natera.com email domain ONLY. Email communications from all other domain names are not from Natera or its employees and are fraudulent. Natera does not request interviews via text messages and does not ask for personal information until a candidate has engaged with the company and has spoken to a recruiter and the hiring team. Natera takes cyber crimes seriously, and will collaborate with law enforcement authorities to prosecute any related cyber crimes.

title: Publication Ethics Associate Editor - 12 Month FTC
description:
*This position is fully remote/home based. Applications will be accepted from candidates based in the UK and the following US states: FL, IL, MA, MD, NY, PA, TX, VA. This is a 12 month FTC position. 

 

Role Summary

The PLOS Publication Ethics team works to uphold the integrity and reliability of PLOS publications and supports PLOS journals in publication ethics-related issues and policy development. The team also engages with external parties and organizations in publication ethics-related discussions and initiatives.
 

We are hiring an Associate Editor on the Publication Ethics team. This role’s primary responsibility is to investigate and resolve publication ethics cases involving PLOS journal content. Cases may be raised before or after publication, and may centre on scientific, ethics, or policy compliance issues (e.g., image integrity issues, animal/human research ethics concerns, data ownership issues, etc.). You will also support PLOS journal editors in their publication ethics work, contribute to Publication Ethics team projects and initiatives (e.g. efforts to improve detection and/or resolution of publication ethics issues), and contribute to other team-level efforts to address ethics and integrity issues at PLOS.

You will report to a Senior Editor, Team Manager for the PLOS Publication Ethics team.

Responsibilities

  • Resolve publication ethics cases efficiently and in line with PLOS standards and COPE guidance; prevent reputational damage to PLOS journals as feasible.
  • Contribute to triage of incoming publication ethics cases
  • With other Publication Ethics team members, develop workflow and policy updates as needed to optimize detection and/or handling of publication ethics issues.
  • Support journal editors in resolving publication ethics issues that arise during manuscript handling, peer review, or post-publication.
  • Communicate rapidly and effectively about ethics cases with involved/affected stakeholders, including the journal’s editorial leads, Editorial Board members, authors, members of other PLOS teams, and any other parties involved in publication ethics case work.
  • Contribute to internal discussions about publication ethics, research integrity, and related issues in team-level and interdepartmental/cross-team forums.
  • You may be asked to provide cover or support for the team’s operational needs.
  • You may be asked to represent PLOS Publication Ethics at meetings, workshops, and/or other forums relevant to publication ethics and research integrity, or to contribute to outward-facing communications about publication ethics issues.
  • Help to recruit and train for vacant team positions and help to train staff on other PLOS teams in publication ethics case management and standards.
  • Uphold high standards of professionalism in all internal and external communications about publication ethics issues.

Knowledge and Skills

  • Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal
  • Highly organized and efficient self-starter with excellent attention to detail and keen problem-solving and analytical skills
  • A collaborative team player who is comfortable working with a remote team
  • A commitment to open access and research integrity
  • (Preferred) Familiarity with Committee on Publication Ethics (COPE) guidance, aptitude for and/or experience in image forensic analysis

Qualifications

  • Master’s or PhD degree, or equivalent (preferably in a scientific discipline)
  • Demonstrated record of discretion and good judgement
  • (Preferred) Post-graduate research experience in a scientific, clinical, or social sciences discipline
  • (Preferred) 1+ year experience in STM publishing, either in an editorial role or in a publication ethics role with primary case investigation responsibilities

Physical Requirements and Work Environment

  • Prolonged periods stationary at a desk and working on a computer.
  • Some national and international travel may be required.
  • Some flexibility to work across time zones.

 

 

The base salary range we’ve established for these positions is (US): $67,000- $73,500 or (UK) £35,000- £38,000. PLOS also offers a comprehensive benefits package summarized below. 

 

BENEFITS: 

US:

  • 401k with employer match
  • Employee sponsored health, dental and vision insurance (Dental and Vision 100% employer paid)
  • Paid Vacation, 11 public holidays and sick leave
  • Parental leave
  • Birthday and three winter holidays days off
  • Short term and long term disability insurance
  • 2 days paid time off for volunteering per year
  • Fully remote work environment with stipend on joining for home office 

UK: 

  • Private medical insurance 
  • Life assurance 
  • Income protection  
  • Personal accident insurance 
  • Pension with up to 10% employer match 
  • 25 days holidays, market competitive Maternity and Paternity leave 
  • Birthday and three winter holidays days off 
  • 2 days paid time off for volunteering per year 
  • Fully remote work environment with stipend on joining for home office

About PLOS 

Building on a strong legacy of pioneering innovation, PLOS continues to be a catalyst in open science, reimagining models to meet open science principles, removing barriers and promoting inclusion in knowledge creation and sharing, and publishing research outputs that enable everyone to learn from, reuse and build upon scientific knowledge.

Our work is supported by a highly skilled global in-house team, partnerships with local scholarly organizations, and the valued contributions of a diverse, international community of scientific researchers.

We’re committed to equal opportunity

We’re working to create a more equitable system of scientific knowledge and understanding. Removing barriers to inclusion and facilitating broad participation of voices is core to our success, inside and out. 

Beyond accepting distinct perspectives, we seek and support divergent backgrounds among our staff because we know differences strengthen our teams, our work, and our communities. We strongly encourage applicants of all identities to join us as we work towards a future where science is open to all, for all. 

Visit plos.org/careers to learn more.

 

To learn more about how PLOS protects your privacy, see our Employee Privacy Notice.

This seat is the answer. description:
Our Why At Dotmatics 

At Dotmatics, a Siemens company,  we believe science, data, and decision-making must be deeply intertwined for innovation to thrive. Our Portfolio includes Luma, LumaLab Connect, ELN Platform, Graphpad Prism, Geneious, SnapGene, Protein Metrics, OMIQ, FCS Express, LabArchives, NQuery, EasyPanel, SoftGenetics and Virscidian.

We have a vision for a new Lab of the Future that will change the future of scientific research.

We have created the world’s most comprehensive digital science platform – best-of-breed software applications already used by more than 2 million scientists, together in a single ecosystem united by a powerful, flexible enterprise data platform. This is not flat data buried away in digital graveyards. This is dynamic, multi-dimensional decision-making.

Scientific enterprises need a new level of effectiveness to achieve tomorrow’s breakthroughs. Illness will not wait. The biosphere will not wait. We are tireless in our vision, because the time for innovation is now.

Shaping the Future of Science At Dotmatics 

Our global team of more than 800 colleagues are dedicated to supporting our customers in over 180 countries. Together, with our scientific community of users, we accelerate scientific innovation in order to make the world a healthier, cleaner, and safer place to live.

You’ll join a collaborative, global team pushing the boundaries of scientific innovation.  Your ideas and efforts will have a tangible impact, accelerating scientific progress and discovery. We offer a dynamic, remote-friendly environment that fosters high integrity and collaboration, empowering you to excel. Dotmatics is a company built by scientists, for scientists. Combined, we are now the world’s largest cloud-based scientific research R&D platform. We need your help to keep growing and pioneering the future.

We are Science Driven. We are Customer Centric. We are Better Together. 

What do we need

We are seeking an Alliance Partner Manager to lead the technical dimension of our alliances and partnering function for Luma, our AI-Native Multimodal Research Platform for Scientific Intelligence. Sitting at the intersection of business and engineering, you'll own how our platform connects with, integrates into, and creates value alongside the products of our strategic technology partners, such as Databricks and AWS.

This position is based in EMEA, working globally across time zones. It is a senior role with broad scope, where you'll act as the bridge between partner engineering teams and our own product, engineering and commercial organizations, working closely with Sales, Legal, Marketing, Engineering, Product, Support and Pre-Sales, as well as colleagues at Siemens, with room to design and build the technical alliance capability around you.

While the focus is strategic, this remains a hands-on role: you'll need enough technical depth to scope integrations credibly, validate them in sandboxes, and hold your own in a conversation with a partner's engineering team. We're looking for someone with an engineering-minded, "application scientist" type approach — comfortable understanding the technical requirements involved in onboarding a partner, and operating confidently within a large company mindset and environment.

In this role you will get to:

  • Define, build, and execute the technical partner strategy, prioritising which integrations and joint solutions to build, developing and implementing joint go-to-market plans (co-sell, co-build, co-deliver), aligning teams and facilitating sales enablement and training of partners.
  • Own engineering level relationships across partner organisations through effective communication, structured governance and business reviews, and joint business planning.
  • Scope integration feasibility early in partner conversations, translating vague partner asks into clear, buildable technical specifications and setting realistic expectations.
  • Oversee solution architecture, use-case mapping, partner product certification and sandbox / proof-of-concept development to design and validate joint solutions.
  • Engage partners to develop differentiated solutions through joint collaboration, market and competitive analysis, and the creation of joint marketing collateral.
  • Evangelise partnerships internally, working closely with Sales, Legal, Marketing, Engineering, Product, Support and Pre-Sales stakeholders, and with colleagues at Siemens, feeding partner needs into the roadmap and organising collaborative events.
  • Define, track and analyse key partnership metrics, collaborating with partners to optimise performance, and represent Dotmatics/Siemens at alliance and partner conferences and events.
  • Focus specifically on systems integration partners, bringing on partners that will meaningfully increase the bottom line.

We are looking for candidate's who have 7+ years in technology partnerships, alliances, solution architecture or pre-sales engineering, including several years leading strategic technical partner or ISV relationships at enterprise scale. You've built integrations, not just managed them, and you can move fluently between a business review and a whiteboard session with a partner's engineers. You're comfortable operating with a high degree of autonomy on complex, ambiguous pursuits, and you set realistic expectations that engineering can actually deliver on.

Just as importantly, you lead through influence. You can align engineering, marketing and sales teams, internally and across partner organisations, behind a shared plan without direct authority, and you're motivated by building a partnering function and team, not just running one. While not a traditional "sales" person, you're comfortable navigating sales-style conversations, combining technical knowledge with strong relationship management and communication skills.

Given the scientific focus of the Luma platform, experience in scientific software, life sciences, pharmaceuticals, biotechnology or research-focused technology would be particularly valuable. We're interested in candidates who understand the challenges of scientific research, including scientific data, laboratory workflows and the technology platforms that support R&D.

Key Skills:

  • Technical partnership leadership - a proven track record defining and executing partner or alliance strategy with ISVs, technology platforms or system integrators, with measurable partner-sourced or partner-influenced revenue impact.
  • Hands-on integration fluency, including practical depth with APIs, authentication and data-exchange patterns, and the ability to scope, spec and validate integrations through sandboxes and proof-of-concept builds.
  • Joint go-to-market execution - experience developing co-sell, co-build and co-deliver plans, aligning internal and partner teams, facilitating sales enablement and creating the collateral that makes joint solutions land.
  • Executive-level relationship management - comfort owning senior stakeholder relationships across partner organisations, running structured business reviews (QBRs), and resolving conflict constructively when internal and partner priorities clash.
  • Data-driven partner management, with the habit of defining, tracking and analysing partnership KPIs and leading indicators of partner health and acting on them before issues escalate.

You may also have:

  • Experience with cloud marketplaces (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud) or OEM / embedded partnership motions.
  • Experience structuring and negotiating complex commercial and technical agreements alongside legal teams.
  • Familiarity with tiered partner certification programmes.
  • Experience or familiarity with scientific software, life sciences, pharmaceuticals, biotechnology or research-focused technology, including scientific data platforms, laboratory systems or R&D workflows. Experience in another domain-deep industry, such as Oil & Gas or Consumer Packaged Goods (CPG), would also be valuable.

Research shows us the confidence gap and imposter syndrome can get in the way of meeting outstanding candidates, so please don’t hesitate to apply — we’d love to hear from you.

Dotmatics Privacy Notice explains what personal information we may process, where we may process your personal information, our purposes for processing your personal information, and the rights you can exercise over Dotmatics use of your personal information. 

Dotmatics is an equal opportunity employer. We are a welcoming place for everyone, and we do our best to make sure all people feel supported and connected at work.

title: Order Resolution Program Manager
description:
Positition:

The Order Resolution Program Manager builds and leads the Order Resolution Program (ORP), a national program that helps ensure patients receive the testing their physicians have ordered. When an order encounters a barrier, such as an unreachable patient, an incorrect phone number, a patient with unanswered questions about their test, or a step that requires clinic involvement, this role makes sure the right people take the right action so care is not delayed. Many of these patients are navigating a cancer diagnosis, and the program exists to support them and the Patient Coordinators who care for them.

As the program's founding owner, the Program Manager exercises independent judgment to assess the current landscape, resolve complex cases directly, and determine what the program needs to succeed, including whether and how to expand the team. The role is hands-on by design: the Program Manager works open cases alongside Patient Coordinators to understand where and why orders stall, then uses that firsthand insight and program data to set strategy, define standards, and guide leadership decisions.

The Program Manager partners across Patient Services, Territory Managers, Clinical Oncology Specialists, Patient Coordinators, Inside Sales Managers, Regional Directors, and Operations Managers, earning alignment through expertise and sound judgment rather than direct authority.

 

Primary Responsibilities:

Program Strategy & Ownership

  • Own the Order Resolution Program end-to-end across all national regions, independently assessing the current landscape, including case volume, root causes, regional variation, and existing workflows, to determine where patient orders are most at risk of delay.
  • Develop a data-supported program roadmap and staffing recommendation for Patient Services leadership, including headcount requirements, staffing structure, timeline, and whether process or tooling solutions would better serve patients.
  • Define the program operating model, including case ownership, escalation criteria, service timelines, handoff protocols, and quality standards, and adjust it as the program matures.
  • Lead the design of the team structure, role definitions, hiring profile, onboarding, and performance expectations for future team members.

Case Resolution & Patient Care Support

  • Exercise independent judgment to evaluate open ORP cases, determine the root cause of each barrier, and develop a tailored resolution strategy that accounts for the clinical context, the patient's circumstances, and available resources.
  • Work complex and high-priority cases directly, including researching LIMS, paper orders, and patient outreach tools to locate missing or updated contact information, and decide whether a case calls for administrative resolution, clinic education or engagement, or escalation.
  • Partner with Patient Coordinators to support patient outreach, providing guidance on how to approach each case and, where appropriate, connecting with patients directly so that questions about their orders are answered and care can move forward.
  • Determine when to escalate a case to the clinic, engage the field team, or close it, and document the rationale so any subsequent owner can continue seamlessly.
  • Maintain a real-time view of all open cases, including status, owner, next action, and age, and follow up consistently to confirm actions are completed and patients are not left waiting.

Analytics & Performance Reporting

  • Design, build, and maintain the ORP reporting infrastructure, including dashboards, KPI scorecards, and regional trend analysis, and define the metrics used to measure program success.
  • Report regularly to Patient Services leadership on case volume, resolution rates, time to resolution, and order completion outcomes, translating data into clear insights about what is working, what is not, and what should change.
  • Analyze recurring barriers, such as common reasons patients cannot be reached or questions that arise repeatedly, and develop recommendations that reduce the number of patients whose orders require intervention in the first place.

Cross-Functional Leadership & Process Improvement

  • Partner with Territory Managers, Clinical Oncology Specialists, Associate Clinical Oncology Specialists, and Patient Coordinators to set clear expectations, communicate promptly, and share accountability on every open case.
  • Partner with Inside Sales Managers, Regional Directors, and Operations Managers to align program priorities, resolve regional barriers, and ensure teams understand their role in supporting patient orders.
  • Serve as the subject matter expert for ORP, providing guidance and consultation to field and operations partners and developing best practices, training, and standard work that can be adopted nationally.
  • Identify systemic process gaps and bring structured, data-backed recommendations to leadership, including changes to workflows, status definitions, tooling, and cross-team handoffs, with the patient experience as the guiding lens.
  • Performs other duties as assigned.

 

Qualifications:

 

  • Bachelor's degree in healthcare administration, business, life sciences, or a related field; or equivalent professional experience in a role requiring independent judgment, program ownership, and decision-making in a healthcare or clinical operations environment.
  • 5 or more years of experience in healthcare operations, patient services, program or project management, or a comparable environment, with demonstrated ownership of a program, workflow, or initiative from assessment through execution.
  • Demonstrated ability to assess a complex operating landscape, identify root causes, and develop and present a data-supported recommendation, including resourcing and staffing needs, to senior leadership.
  • Proven ability to independently assess multi-variable situations and determine the appropriate course of action without direct supervision, particularly in patient-facing or clinically sensitive contexts.
  • Demonstrated ability to influence and drive accountability across cross-functional teams, including field, sales, and operations leaders, without direct authority.
  • Strong analytical capability, including building performance reporting, interpreting trends, and communicating findings clearly to leadership; advanced MS Excel or equivalent skills required.
  • Experience in a call center, patient outreach, or high-volume case management environment (inbound and outbound).
  • Proficiency in CRM platforms, case tracking systems, and data tools; familiarity with skip tracing tools and LIMS is a strong plus.
  • Prior experience leading, coaching, or building a team is preferred. Background in patient coordination or another patient-facing healthcare role is strongly preferred.

 

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

Technical

  • Program and project management expertise, including scoping, planning, prioritization, milestone tracking, and stakeholder management.
  • Specialized knowledge of healthcare operations, patient services workflows, and clinical coordination sufficient to evaluate case scenarios and develop resolution strategies without relying on standardized scripts.
  • Advanced proficiency in CRM platforms, case tracking systems, and reporting tools, with the ability to design KPI dashboards that give leadership real-time visibility into program performance and patient order outcomes.
  • Strong quantitative skills, including comfort working with large data sets to identify trends, build business cases, and model staffing and capacity needs.
  • Experience with skip tracing tools and multi-database research methods, and with process documentation and standard operating procedure development.

Behavioral

  • Exercises sound, independent judgment consistently, treating each case and each program decision as a situation requiring individualized analysis.
  • Builds before being asked: sees what a new program needs, takes ownership of the decision, and moves forward without waiting to be told something is off track.
  • Balances urgency and care: moves quickly because patients are waiting, and makes thoughtful decisions because the stakes are real.
  • Thinks like a program owner and acts like a teammate: comfortable working individual cases to learn the work, and equally comfortable stepping back to set strategy and advise leadership.
  • Earns credibility with cross-functional partners through expertise, clear communication, and follow-through, and uses it to drive action across teams they do not directly control.
  • Coaches and develops others, and is ready to build and lead a team as the program grows.

 

Physical Demands & Work Environment:

  • This is a primarily remote position. Occasional on-site attendance may be required for planning sessions, leadership reviews, or business needs.
  • Duties are performed in a home office or professional office setting and require the ability to use a computer keyboard, communicate over the telephone, and read printed and digital material.
  • This role may require working outside standard business hours at times to address time-sensitive case situations or program needs.

Travel:

Minimal travel required. Occasional travel (estimated less than 15%) may be required for national leadership meetings, regional business reviews, or planning sessions.

description:
130.000 Fahrzeuge im Jahr. Sechs Länder. Hinter jeder Transaktion stecken Fahrzeugbewertungen, Kapazitätsplanung und Routenoptimierung, Prozesse, die bei CarOnSale gerade aktiv skaliert werden. CarOnSale ist die KI-gestützte Plattform für den B2B-Gebrauchtwagenhandel in Europa. Über 40.000 Käufer aus mehr als 20 Ländern handeln auf unserer Plattform – und 85 % des Inventars ist exklusiv bei uns. One Platform. One Profit Engine.

  • Prozessoptimierung: Du unterstützt die Weiterentwicklung unserer Inspection- und Dispatching-Prozesse und hilfst, sie effizienter und skalierbarer zu machen.
  • Datenbasierte Analyse: Du unterstützt bei der Analyse bestehender Abläufe, etwa Routeneffizienz, Termin-Auslastung und Qualitätsraten, und hilfst, Verbesserungsmaßnahmen abzuleiten.
  • KI und Automatisierung: Du lernst unsere KI-Tools kennen und wirkst beim Aufbau von Automatisierungen und Agents mit, die echte operative Probleme lösen.
  • Reporting: Du hilfst beim Erstellen von Präsentationen und Reportings, mit denen Performance-Kennzahlen und strategische Initiativen ans Management gehen.
  • Teamarbeit: Du arbeitest eng mit Team-Leads, Disponenten und dem Ops-Management zusammen und begleitest laufende Projekte.

 

Was du mitbringst

Must-have

  • Studium in BWL, Wirtschaftswissenschaften, (Wirtschafts-)Ingenieurwesen, Logistik, Data oder einem verwandten Bereich, oder Abschluss bereits in der Tasche
  • Analytisches und strukturiertes Denken kombiniert mit einer Hands-on-Mentalität
  • Sicherer Umgang mit Zahlen und Daten; Excel und PowerPoint sind selbstverständlich
  • KI-affine Arbeitsweise, du nutzt Tools wie Claude, ChatGPT oder Gemini aktiv im Alltag
  • Deutsch C1 und Englisch C1, beide Sprachen gehören zum Arbeitsalltag

Nice to have

  • Erste Erfahrung im Consulting, Business Development, Operations oder einem datengetriebenen Umfeld
  • SQL oder erste Erfahrung mit BI-Tools
  • Interesse an oder Erfahrung mit der Automobilbranche

 

Was dich bei uns erwartet

  • Strukturiertes Onboarding mit Buddy-Programm
  • Regelmäßige Feedbackzyklen
  • Frisches Obst und Getränke im Büro
  • Laptop für mobiles Arbeiten
  • Gelebte Vielfalt: aktives Frauennetzwerk, Meditations- & Gebetsraum

 

Wir besetzen aktuell mehrere Praktika im Operations-Umfeld. Wenn sich im Gespräch zeigt, dass ein anderer Bereich besser zu dir passt, sprechen wir darüber.

 

Bewirb dich jetzt – dein Lebenslauf reicht.

POSITION SUMMARY:  On site position in Austin, TX

The Accessioning Team Runner collects, sorts, and transports packages to Accessioning laboratory in the Austin, TX office.  Hourly rate is $17.

Monday-Friday, 9am-530pm
Hourly rate starts at $17

 

 PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Sort and transport packages from the Shipping dock to the Accessioning laboratory.

  • Pick up packages from the receptionist’s desk.

  • Scan all tracking numbers into a Google spreadsheet and ensure that tracking numbers are scanned in correctly and spreadsheet is filled out completely.

  • Distribute packages to the Clinical Data Operators (CDO) in a timely and efficient manner following distribution guidelines.

  • Rack samples that arrive in bulk (without individual kit boxes) ensuring that the paperwork matches up with the samples.

  • Escalate any issues or discrepancies to the Leads or Supervisor.

  • Empty biohazard cans in the lab.

  • Scan bench worksheets.

  • Scan documents into cases.

  • Maintain tidiness of Runner workstations.

  • Store requisition forms by date into the filing cabinets.

  • Dispose of requisition forms into the shred bins that have exceeded the retention period.

  • Performs other duties as assigned.

  • Notify Supervisor and Leads of any packaging issues or discrepancies

  • This role works with PHI on a regular basis both in paper and electronic form and has access to various technologies to access PHI (paper and electronic) in order to perform the job

  • Employee must complete training relating to HIPAA/PHI privacy, General Policies and Procedure Compliance training and security training as soon as possible but not later than the first 30 days of hire.

  • Must maintain a current status on Natera training requirements.

 

  • QUALIFICATIONS

  • High School Diploma (or equivalent) required.

  • Ability to work quickly and efficiently.

title: EH&S Lead
description:
About Arc Institute

Arc Institute is an independent nonprofit research organization at the interface of artificial intelligence and biology, working to accelerate scientific progress and understand the root causes of complex diseases. Founded in 2021 and based in Palo Alto, Arc partners with Stanford University, UC Berkeley, and UC San Francisco.

Unlike academia, our scientists have long-term funding and industry-like resources. Unlike industry, they're free to pursue high-risk, long-term research without commercial pressures. Arc's Technology Centers and Core Investigator labs work side by side, integrating experimental and computational biology under one roof to tackle problems neither could solve alone.

Our two Institute Initiatives reflect this model in action:

  • Virtual Cell Initiative: Building a full-stack virtual cell model to identify disease mechanisms and nominate drug targets,  accelerating the path from biological insight to clinical trials.
  • Alzheimer's Disease Initiative: Mapping the genes, pathways, and environmental factors behind Alzheimer's disease to develop drug candidates that address root causes.

More than 300 Arconauts work together at our Palo Alto headquarters, backed by substantial long-term philanthropic funding.

About the position

As EH&S Lead, you will own the development, implementation, and the management of Arc’s Environmental, Health, and Safety programs and culture. You will design solutions that satisfy overlapping local, state, and federal requirements, and serve as Arc’s primary point of contact for regulatory and certifying agencies.

Your remit covers chemical hygiene, biosafety, OSHA compliance, medical and hazardous waste, and Arc’s safety permits and sustainability programs. You will hire and manage a biosafety manager and direct the work of outside vendors and consultants.

About you

  • You are deeply committed to the health and safety of your colleagues, and you achieve it through partnership with the labs rather than around them.
  • You are genuinely curious about the science here and want to understand the research at a real level of depth.
  • You thrive in a diverse environment and enjoy working with scientists and students from many backgrounds.
  • You are energized by building programs and forging cross-functional partnerships that strengthen the community and the mission.

In this position you will

  • Provide safety leadership and EH&S subject matter expertise aligned with Arc’s operating principles.
  • Develop, implement, and maintain EH&S programs, procedures, and systems in compliance with federal, state, and local regulations, driving continuous improvement.
  • Develop Arc’s safety strategy and carry out safety policies and procedures in accordance with all applicable regulatory and organizational requirements.
  • Hire, manage, and develop a biosafety manager, setting clear priorities and standards for their work.
  • Advise Arc’s administrative team on safety and compliance for specific projects and operations.
  • Define Arc’s approach to  EH&S employee safety and onboarding training, with a focus on efficiency and engagement.
  • Own and evolve Arc’s compliance programs including, but not limited to, the Cal/OSHA bloodborne pathogens standard and biosafety program, chemical safety, radiation safety, and controlled substances.
  • Own Arc’s environmental compliance strategy, including the industrial wastewater discharge permit, hazardous waste requirements, and regulatory permitting.
  • Own risk assessment program and conduct regular risk assessments and safety audits to identify workplace hazards — chemical, physical, biological, industrial, and radiological among them — and remediate hazards or recommend improvements to reduce them.
  • Lead investigations of accidents, incidents, injuries, and complaints concerning potential hazards or unsafe conditions to determine root causes and preventive measures.
  • Conduct safety inspections and walkthroughs that deliver meaningful insight and surface continuous improvement opportunities across Arc’s labs.
